_meta.purpose: Phase 2 Tranche C part 3d, Stage 1: labeled eval question set ONLY. No harness, no runs, no threshold tuning happen against this file yet -- it is a proposal for human review before it becomes the basis for tuning SEMANTIC_MATCH_THRESHOLD or comparing FTS vs semantic retrieval.
_meta.status: PROPOSED, NOT YET APPROVED -- labels are the author's (Claude's) best judgment, not ground truth. Push back on any label before it is used for anything.
_meta.corpus: 4 topics x 2 languages x 4 chunks = 32 chunks, agency 56fbfe38, seeded in 20260902130000_seed_knowledge_base_probe.sql

dementia_sop.title_en: Dementia Care Support — Standard Operating Procedure
dementia_sop.title_es: Atención a Clientes con Demencia — Procedimiento Operativo Estándar

topics.none: Out-of-domain or should-refuse -- no document in the corpus should ground this question.

categories.answerable: Clear hit in exactly one document. May optionally carry a near_miss_document -- see that field's own note -- for a question whose primary intent is clear but which plausibly also scores close on a second, related document; the eval measures that gap rather than presuming ambiguity.
categories.ambiguous: Genuinely spans two documents -- expected_document is an array of two topic keys. The question's own phrasing doesn't disambiguate which document the asker means, and both documents contain content that legitimately answers a plausible reading of it. Reserved for questions that explicitly invoke both topics' concepts (see q18/q20's construction) -- a question that merely COULD near-miss a second document without naming it belongs in answerable with near_miss_document instead (see q17).
categories.out_of_domain: A real caregiver question the KB has no content for at all -- no lexical or topical overlap with any document. Tests plain refusal. CAVEAT: these labels are relative to the CURRENT 4-document seed corpus only. Once real agency documents are ingested (Phase 1G), several of these (mileage, overtime, benefits enrollment, direct deposit) could become genuinely answerable if a real agency's HR/payroll policies happen to cover them -- this question set will need relabeling against whatever corpus it's actually run against at that point, not reused unchanged.
categories.misleading: Shares vocabulary or an adjacent concept with a real document but is NOT actually answered by it -- the FTS-failure class (stem collisions, adjacent-topic word overlap). Must refuse (expected_document: none) despite the surface-level pull toward a real document. Same Phase 1G relabeling caveat as out_of_domain applies.

questions.question: What's the call-off policy?
questions.rationale: Names the policy directly -- the easy, unambiguous case.

questions.question: How far in advance do I need to tell my scheduler I can't work a shift?
questions.rationale: Paraphrases chunk 0 ('notify your scheduler as far in advance as possible... no later than two hours before').

questions.question: ¿Cuál es la política de ausencias?
questions.rationale: Direct Spanish equivalent of q01, unambiguous.

questions.question: ¿A quién llamo si estoy enfermo y no puedo trabajar mi turno?
questions.rationale: Maps to ES chunks 1 (call the on-call line) and 3 (sick policy, call off immediately).

questions.question: How much PTO do I get?
questions.rationale: Required FTS-failure-pair case (paired with q06) -- both phrasings of the same intent must answer, not just one.

questions.question: How many hours of PTO do I earn?
questions.rationale: Required pair with q05 -- this exact phrasing is the one Phase 1's FTS probe already answered correctly (rank 0.040); q05 is the one a caregiver would more naturally ask.

questions.question: ¿Cuántas horas de PTO puedo acumular?
questions.rationale: From the original Phase 1 bilingual probe -- confirmed answerable in Spanish (docs/phase-1-fts-results.md, rank 0.047).

questions.question: ¿Puedo cobrar mi PTO si renuncio por mi cuenta?
questions.rationale: Maps to chunk 2 (not paid out upon voluntary resignation) -- tests understanding of the payout/rollover rule, not just accrual.

questions.question: How should I respond if a client with dementia gets confused about what day it is?
questions.rationale: Maps to chunk 1 (don't argue or correct, gently redirect).

questions.question: What should I do if my client tries to wander outside?
questions.rationale: Maps to chunk 2 (wandering, exterior doors, redirect vs. physically blocking).

questions.question: ¿Cómo debo reaccionar si un cliente con demencia se confunde sobre dónde está?
questions.rationale: Spanish equivalent of q09, maps to ES chunk 1.

questions.question: ¿Qué debo anotar si noto que el comportamiento de un cliente ha cambiado?
questions.rationale: Maps to ES chunk 3 (document behavioral changes, notify scheduler).

questions.question: Can I open my client's pill organizer to sort their medication?
questions.rationale: Maps to chunk 0 (must never open, count, sort, or handle bottles directly) -- answer is 'no', but the document is clearly the right source.

questions.question: What should I do if a client refuses to take their medicine?
questions.rationale: Maps to chunk 2 (refusal handling, note it, inform scheduler).

questions.question: ¿Puedo administrar una inyección a mi cliente?
questions.rationale: Maps to ES chunk 1 (no injections, patches, or medical-judgment tasks).

questions.question: ¿Qué hago si las pastillas de un cliente parecen haber sido manipuladas?
questions.rationale: Maps to ES chunk 3 (tampered/incorrect pills, contact scheduler, don't fix it yourself).

questions.question: I can't make my shift, what do I do?
questions.rationale: RELABELED per review: primary intent reads as not attending at all (call-off), not as leaving a shift already in progress -- unlike q18/q20, it doesn't explicitly invoke both concepts, so labeling it ambiguous would presume the answer the eval is meant to measure. Labeled answerable-primary with pto_policy as an expected near-miss so Stage 2 measures the actual score gap between the two documents for this exact phrasing (the live-observed 3c near-miss) instead of assuming ambiguity a priori. A small measured gap becomes evidence for a disambiguation trigger; a large gap confirms this is retrieval imprecision, not genuine ambiguity.

questions.question: If I can't work my shift, should I call off or use my time off?
questions.rationale: Deliberately juxtaposes both concepts in one question -- constructed to be unambiguously ambiguous, testing whether retrieval surfaces both top documents rather than arbitrarily picking one.

questions.question: No puedo terminar mi turno, ¿qué hago?
questions.rationale: RELABELED per review, for consistency with q17's rule: doesn't explicitly invoke both concepts. 'Terminar' specifically means finish/complete, unambiguously implying the shift is already in progress -- primary intent is PTO's 'leave a shift early' framing (chunk 3), with call_off_policy as the expected near-miss. A deliberate mirror of q17: same structural near-miss pattern, opposite primary document, strengthening the eval's ability to measure the gap in both directions.

questions.question: Si no puedo hacer mi turno, ¿debo avisar o puedo usar tiempo libre?
questions.rationale: Spanish equivalent of q18, explicitly naming both 'avisar' (call off) and 'tiempo libre' (PTO).

questions.question: Can I adjust my client's medication schedule if they seem confused?
questions.rationale: Combines dementia-confusion framing with a medication-adjustment question -- Dementia SOP chunk 3 explicitly says don't adjust medication timing/dosage, and Medication Guidelines is the document actually about medication handling. Both are legitimately relevant.

questions.question: My client with dementia refuses their pills -- what should I do?
questions.rationale: Spans Dementia SOP's behavioral/redirect guidance and Medication Guidelines chunk 2 (refusal handling) -- arguably both are correct answers.

questions.question: ¿Puedo cambiar la dosis de medicamento si mi cliente con demencia está agitado?
questions.rationale: Spanish equivalent of q21.

questions.question: Mi cliente con demencia no quiere tomar sus pastillas, ¿qué hago?
questions.rationale: Spanish equivalent of q22.

questions.question: How do I enroll in the agency's health insurance benefits?

questions.question: Which app do I use to clock in and out for my shifts?

questions.question: Do I get reimbursed for mileage when driving between client visits?

questions.question: How do I complete my annual background check renewal?

questions.question: How do I set up direct deposit?
questions.rationale: REQUIRED case. FTS false-matched the Medication chunk via a 'directly'->'direct' stem collision (docs/phase-1-fts-results.md). No direct-deposit content exists anywhere -- must refuse. Tests whether cosine avoids the same trap via meaning rather than stems.

questions.question: What's the overtime pay rate for working a holiday shift?
questions.rationale: From the original Phase 1 probe (FTS rank 0.015, correctly refused via the shared word 'pay' with PTO). No overtime/pay-rate content exists in PTO or anywhere else -- must refuse. Tests whether cosine's semantic 'compensation' clustering incorrectly pulls this toward PTO despite no real answer existing.

questions.question: Is call-off pay available if I get sent home early?
questions.rationale: Deliberately blends call-off and pay/compensation vocabulary from two real topics, but neither document discusses a 'call-off pay' concept -- must refuse. Tests whether blended vocabulary from two real topics false-grounds on one of them.
